topics.label: Big-O Notation
topics.desc: Asymptotic upper-bound notation for growth rate, the lingua franca for comparing algorithm time and space costs at scale.

topics.label: Asymptotic Bounds
topics.desc: The Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta family giving upper, lower, and tight bounds that formalize growth-rate comparisons.

topics.label: Amortized Analysis
topics.desc: Averaging cost over a sequence of operations so occasional expensive steps (like array resizes) are charged fairly.

topics.label: Recurrence Relations
topics.desc: Equations expressing an algorithm's cost in terms of subproblems, the standard tool for analyzing recursive procedures.

topics.label: Master Theorem
topics.desc: A cookbook for solving divide-and-conquer recurrences of form T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) without unrolling them by hand.

topics.label: P, NP & Reductions
topics.desc: The P/NP/NP-complete hierarchy and polynomial reductions that classify which problems are tractable versus intractable.

topics.label: Space Complexity
topics.desc: Memory consumed as a function of input size, including auxiliary space and the often-overlooked recursion-stack cost.

topics.label: Dynamic Arrays
topics.desc: Contiguous resizable arrays with amortized O(1) append, the cache-friendly default sequence in most languages.

topics.label: Linked Lists
topics.desc: Node-and-pointer sequences giving O(1) splice but poor locality, foundational for many pointer-based structures.

topics.label: Stack
topics.desc: LIFO structure underpinning recursion, expression evaluation, backtracking, and depth-first traversal.

topics.label: Queue
topics.desc: FIFO structure central to breadth-first search, buffering, and scheduling; often backed by a ring buffer.

topics.label: Deque
topics.desc: Double-ended queue allowing O(1) push/pop at both ends, enabling sliding-window and monotonic-queue techniques.

topics.label: Hash Tables
topics.desc: Key-value store with expected O(1) lookup via hashing and collision resolution, the workhorse of associative access.

topics.label: Circular Buffer
topics.desc: Fixed-size ring with wraparound indices for bounded FIFO streaming, common in producer-consumer and I/O buffering.

topics.label: Binary Trees
topics.desc: Hierarchical structure with at most two children per node, the basis for search trees, heaps, and traversal algorithms.

topics.label: Tree Traversal
topics.desc: In/pre/post-order and level-order visitation patterns that systematically enumerate every node of a tree.

topics.label: Binary Search Trees
topics.desc: Ordered tree giving O(log n) search/insert/delete when balanced, the conceptual root of ordered-map structures.

topics.label: Balanced BSTs
topics.desc: Self-rebalancing trees like AVL and red-black that guarantee O(log n) height via rotations under all updates.

topics.label: Binary Heap
topics.desc: Array-backed complete tree giving O(log n) priority-queue operations, the standard implementation behind heapsort.

topics.label: B-Trees
topics.desc: High-fanout balanced trees minimizing disk seeks, the indexing backbone of databases and filesystems.

topics.label: Trie
topics.desc: Prefix tree storing strings by shared prefixes, enabling fast autocomplete, dictionary, and prefix-query operations.

topics.label: Graph Representation
topics.desc: Adjacency-list versus adjacency-matrix encodings whose choice drives the time and space cost of every graph algorithm.

topics.label: Breadth-First Search
topics.desc: Queue-driven level-order graph exploration computing shortest paths in unweighted graphs and connectivity.

topics.label: Depth-First Search
topics.desc: Stack/recursion-driven traversal exposing tree edges, cycles, and discovery times for many graph decompositions.

topics.label: Topological Sort
topics.desc: Linear ordering of a DAG respecting all dependencies, essential for scheduling, build systems, and DAG-based DP.

topics.label: Shortest Paths
topics.desc: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, and Floyd-Warshall computing minimum-cost routes under various weight and negativity constraints.

topics.label: Minimum Spanning Tree
topics.desc: Kruskal and Prim algorithms finding a least-weight connecting subgraph, classic greedy applications on graphs.

topics.label: Strongly Connected Components
topics.desc: Tarjan/Kosaraju decomposition of a digraph into mutually reachable groups, used in dependency and 2-SAT analysis.

topics.label: Union-Find
topics.desc: Disjoint-set forest with path compression giving near-constant connectivity queries, key to Kruskal and clustering.

topics.label: Divide & Conquer
topics.desc: Splitting a problem into independent subproblems and combining results, the paradigm behind mergesort and FFT.

topics.label: Dynamic Programming
topics.desc: Solving overlapping subproblems once and reusing results via memoization or tabulation over an optimal substructure.

topics.label: Greedy Algorithms
topics.desc: Building solutions via locally optimal choices, correct only when a matroid or exchange-argument structure holds.

topics.label: Backtracking
topics.desc: Systematic DFS over a constraint search space with pruning, the engine for combinatorial generation and CSPs.

topics.label: Branch & Bound
topics.desc: Backtracking enhanced with bounding functions to prune subtrees that cannot beat the best known optimum.

topics.label: Two Pointers & Sliding Window
topics.desc: Coordinated index movement over sequences to solve subarray and pair problems in linear time without nesting.

topics.label: Recursion
topics.desc: Self-referential problem decomposition with base and recursive cases, the conceptual foundation of most design techniques.

topics.label: Comparison Sorts
topics.desc: Quicksort, mergesort, and heapsort bounded by the O(n log n) comparison lower bound, the standard general sorters.

topics.label: Linear-Time Sorts
topics.desc: Counting, radix, and bucket sort exploiting key structure to beat O(n log n) when inputs have bounded range.

topics.label: Sorting Lower Bound
topics.desc: The decision-tree argument proving any comparison sort needs Omega(n log n) comparisons in the worst case.

topics.label: Binary Search
topics.desc: Halving a sorted search space for O(log n) lookup, generalizable to monotonic predicates and answer-space search.

topics.label: Selection & Order Statistics
topics.desc: Quickselect and median-of-medians finding the k-th smallest element in expected or worst-case linear time.

topics.label: Stability & In-Place Sorting
topics.desc: Properties governing whether equal keys keep order and whether sorting uses O(1) extra space, driving algorithm choice.

topics.label: String Matching
topics.desc: Locating a pattern within text via KMP, Boyer-Moore, or Rabin-Karp, the core of search and grep-style tools.

topics.label: KMP Algorithm
topics.desc: Linear-time matching using a failure function that skips redundant comparisons after a partial match.

topics.label: Rolling Hash
topics.desc: Constant-time sliding hash over substrings powering Rabin-Karp matching and fast substring fingerprint comparison.

topics.label: Suffix Trees & Arrays
topics.desc: Indexes over all suffixes enabling fast substring, longest-common, and repeat queries on large texts.

topics.label: Edit Distance
topics.desc: DP measuring minimum insert/delete/substitute operations between strings, basis of diffing and spell correction.

topics.label: Aho-Corasick
topics.desc: Multi-pattern matcher building a trie with failure links to scan text for many keywords in a single pass.

topics.label: Segment Trees
topics.desc: Tree over array ranges giving O(log n) range queries and point updates, often with lazy propagation for range updates.

topics.label: Fenwick Tree
topics.desc: Binary indexed tree giving compact O(log n) prefix-sum queries and updates with minimal code and memory.

topics.label: Bloom Filter
topics.desc: Probabilistic membership structure with no false negatives, trading tiny false-positive rates for huge space savings.

topics.label: Skip List
topics.desc: Layered randomized linked list giving expected O(log n) ordered operations, a simpler alternative to balanced trees.

topics.label: LRU Cache
topics.desc: Hash-map plus doubly linked list giving O(1) get/put with least-recently-used eviction, a ubiquitous caching design.

topics.label: Network Flow
topics.desc: Max-flow/min-cut algorithms like Ford-Fulkerson modeling matching, assignment, and capacity-constrained routing.
